description: Verifies the equations of state and the stellar structure solver: ideal gas, Synge and Mathews relations and limits, the degenerate Fermi gas identities, the tabulated nuclear table round trip, and Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff stars for a white dwarf, a free neutron gas and the SFHo, Shen and LS220 tables.

checks.label: the pressure equals (Gamma - 1) rho eps
the specific internal energy is recovered
the specific enthalpy equals 1 + eps + p / rho
the sound speed squared equals Gamma p / (rho h)
the sound speed squared is positive and below Gamma - 1
the cold Synge enthalpy approaches the non-relativistic limit 1 + 5/2 theta
the hot Synge enthalpy approaches the ultra-relativistic limit 4 theta within 5 percent
the cold Mathews sound speed squared lies in (0, 1/3)
the hot Mathews sound speed squared approaches 1/3
the energy density exceeds the pressure
the specific enthalpy equals sqrt(1 + x^2)
the sound speed squared equals c^2 x^2 / (3 (1 + x^2))
the density is recovered from the pressure within a relative 1e-8
the pressure is recovered from the enthalpy within a relative 1e-8
the preset carries the SFHo name
the pressure at 3e17 kg/m^3 is positive
the sound speed squared is positive and causal
the table survives the container round trip
the pressure survives the round trip within a relative 1e-10
the sound speed survives the round trip within 1e-10
the white dwarf integration converges
the white dwarf mass lies between 0.5 and the Chandrasekhar limit 1.44 solar masses
the white dwarf radius lies between 1000 and 20000 km
the white dwarf compactness is below 1e-3
the maximum mass of a free neutron gas lies near the Oppenheimer-Volkoff value of 0.7 solar masses
the radius at the maximum mass lies between 8 and 12 km
the SFHo maximum mass lies between 1.95 and 2.15 solar masses
the SFHo radius at the maximum mass lies between 9 and 13 km
the SFHo radius of a 1.4 solar mass star lies between 10.5 and 14 km
the Shen maximum mass lies between 2.05 and 2.30 solar masses
the LS220 maximum mass lies between 1.95 and 2.15 solar masses
the stiffer Shen equation of state supports a larger maximum mass than LS220
